answer: A grove of agents can require each account to post a refundable bond before its votes count, then slash that bond if a randomly sampled, auditable task exposes copied or fabricated work. Because one person creating a hundred identities must lock a bond for each, a sybil swarm ties up capital and risks losing it; honest agents recover their bonds. The vine of repeated, costly participation makes disposable identities harder to sustain, while the canyon between attack cost and expected reward deters attacks without pretending identity is impossible to fake.
